subject: Physics
description: SI base units, derived units, prefixes, dimensional analysis

questions.stem: The SI base unit of temperature is the:
questions.explanation: Kelvin (K) — one of the seven SI base units. Starts at absolute zero (−273.15 °C). Named after Lord Kelvin (William Thomson). The seven SI base units are — metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance), candela (luminous intensity). Celsius is a SI derived unit; Fahrenheit is the US customary scale.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The SI unit of energy is the:
questions.explanation: Joule (J) — SI unit of energy and work. 1 J = 1 N·m (force × distance). Named after James Prescott Joule. Watt (W) = J/s — unit of power (energy per unit time). Newton — force; Pascal — pressure (N/m²). 1 food calorie = 4,184 J; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The SI prefix 'giga' denotes a factor of:
questions.explanation: SI prefixes — kilo (10³), mega (10⁶), giga (10⁹), tera (10¹²), peta (10¹⁵), exa (10¹⁸). And the opposites — milli (10⁻³), micro (10⁻⁶), nano (10⁻⁹), pico (10⁻¹²), femto (10⁻¹⁵), atto (10⁻¹⁸). So 1 GHz = 10⁹ Hz, 1 GB = 10⁹ bytes.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: One 'light year' is a unit of:
questions.explanation: Light year — the distance light travels in a vacuum in one year ≈ 9.461 × 10¹² km ≈ 9.46 trillion km. Used in astronomy for interstellar distances. The nearest star system (Alpha Centauri) is ~4.24 ly away. Other astronomical distance units — parsec (~3.26 ly), astronomical unit (AU ≈ 1.496 × 10⁸ km, the Earth-Sun distance).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
questions.explanation: Coulomb (C) — 1 C = 1 A × 1 s, the charge that flows past a point in a conductor per second at a current of 1 ampere. Named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb. Electron's charge e ≈ 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Ampere — current; volt — potential difference; watt — power. Capacitance is farad (C/V).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Force = mass × acceleration. Dimensions — [M] × [L T⁻²] = [M L T⁻²]. Energy / work = force × distance = [M L² T⁻²]. Pressure = force / area = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Momentum = mass × velocity = [M L T⁻¹]. Useful for dimensional-analysis checks — both sides of any physical equation must have the same dimensions.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: 1 mechanical horsepower ≈ 745.7 W (~746 W). Metric horsepower (PS) ≈ 735.5 W. Both stem from James Watt's estimate of a horse's sustained power output. Car engines are rated in hp (100-400 hp for typical passenger cars). 1 kW ≈ 1.34 hp. A fit human can sustain ~0.1 hp for long periods.
